title.narrative: Promoting gender equality with church partners

description.narrative:
Gender inequality in Kenya has mainly been perpetuated by poor policies at both the national level and at the local level, including the Catholic church. Women’s contribution to the economy has been grossly unrecognized, a factor which has led to ineffective development of policies since in actual sense women perform 2/3 of the workload.
The Catholic Church in Kenya did an evaluation on its Women and Gender Development programme (WGDP) in 2003.The report identified gender mainstreaming as a cross cutting issue in development. It was realized that there can be no meaningful development without addressing the pressing gender concerns.
The Kenya Episcopal conference adopted the churh gender policy in November 2011.This landmark policy,though not to the standard of any good gender policy is a pointer of the positive steps that the Catholic church in Kenya is willing to engender its programmes.It is also the first policy of its kind.
The proposal therefore seeks to clearly identify and bridge the gender disparities in understanding and in programme implementation by the Catholic church . Alongside this the proposal seeks to support CARITAS Kenya to push roll out the gender policy document for the Kenya Catholic church and to fund CARITAS Kenya to do gender training in three pilot dioceses.
The project shall amongs many other things:-
• Undertake a gender audit in two dioceses in order to contextualize and recommend to the church the gaps and opportunities available in each diocese being mindfull of the cultural sensitivities in these dioceses as well as bring out lessons that can move forward the engerndering of projects within our partners as well as allighning to tthe organization’s gender global strategy. • To Lobby the Kenya Episcopal conference, through the more open minded Bishops to support CARITAS initiative in rolling out the gender strategy. • Support CARITAS Kenya to carry out gender trainings and mentoring in three pilot dioceses in Kenya,carrry out exchange visits,develop a gender audit checklist and carry out women and girls specific trainings. • CAFOD to build / strengthen the capacity of its partners on gender as a contribution to gender compliance. • CAFOD, CARITAS and funded partners participate in the 16 days of activism against violence against women for the first time. • Have a learning meeting of all the CAFOD gender network meeting in Nairobi to evaluate the mainstreaming of gender amongst partners and within CAFOD.
The initiative has identified Gender, Environment and sustainable Development (GESD) based on its experience of working with the Catholic church on gender issues to help carry out the gender audit and the TOT trainings in the dioceses.
